title: Integral closure of a nondegenerate quadratic formal plane curve
statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $a,b,c\in F$ satisfy $a\ne0$ and $b^2-4ac\ne0$. Put
$$R=F[[X,Y]]/(aX^2+bXY+cY^2),\qquad L=F[Z]/(aZ^2+bZ+c),$$
write $z$ for the class of $Z$ in $L$, and write $x,y$ for the classes of $X,Y$ in $R$. Polynomial rings, power series, and algebra quotients are [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The substitution $x\mapsto zt$, $y\mapsto t$ defines an injective $F$-algebra map
$$j:R\hookrightarrow L[[t]]$$
whose image is exactly $F+tL[[t]]$, where $F$ is embedded by constant series. The ring $R$ is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotents); its total ring of fractions $Q(R)$ is the localization obtained by inverting every non-zero-divisor. The ring $L[[t]]$ is finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $j$ identifies it with the integral closure of $R$ in $Q(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Under this identification the extension of $(x,y)$ is $tL[[t]]$, and $y=t$ is a non-zero-divisor. All identifications respect the displayed map $j$.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, Case I and Case II, with X and Y interchanged in Case II; the common presentation using the separable quadratic algebra includes the split product case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-quadratic-homogeneous-substitution] to $F,a,b,c$. It constructs the specified coefficientwise substitution $j$, proves its injectivity and image $A=F+tB$ for $B=L[[t]]$, and gives $x\mapsto zt$, $y\mapsto t$. Put $\beta=b/a$ and $\gamma=c/a$; multiplying the polynomial relation by $a^{-1}$ identifies the same coefficient algebra with $F[Z]/(Z^2+\beta Z+\gamma)$.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, Case I and Case II, with X and Y interchanged in Case II; the common presentation using the separable quadratic algebra includes the split product case.

proof.text: Since $\beta^2-4\gamma=(b^2-4ac)/a^2\ne0$, [lem-sfb-quadratic-series-field-factors] applies to this $L$. It gives $B\cong\prod_iD_i$ with each $D_i$ an integrally closed domain, reducedness of $B$, two $A$-module generators $1,z$, integrality over $A$ via the stated monic equation, and regularity of $t$. The injection $j$ makes $R$ reduced; its isomorphism onto $A$ transfers the two module generators to the asserted finite $R$-module structure on $B$.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, Case I and Case II, with X and Y interchanged in Case II; the common presentation using the separable quadratic algebra includes the split product case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-regular-conductor-fraction-normalization] to $A\subseteq B\cong\prod_iD_i$ and the element $t$. There are one or two factors, so the product is nonempty. The first step gives $tB\subseteq A$, hence $t=t\cdot1\in A$; the second gives the domain normality, regularity and integrality hypotheses. Its compatible embedding $k(h)=(th)/t$ identifies $B$ with the integral closure of $A$ in $Q(A)$ and identifies $Q(A)$ with $Q(B)$. Explicitly, the isomorphism $j:R\to A$ sends regular elements to regular elements, so the inverse fraction map sends $r/s\in Q(A)$ to $j^{-1}(r)/j^{-1}(s)\in Q(R)$. Composing with $k$ gives $k_R(h)=j^{-1}(th)/y$, since $j(y)=t$. For $h=j(r)$ this is $(yr)/y=r$ in $Q(R)$; transporting a monic equation coefficient by coefficient along $j$ gives the asserted integral-closure equality inside $Q(R)$ with these specified maps.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, Case I and Case II, with X and Y interchanged in Case II; the common presentation using the separable quadratic algebra includes the split product case.

proof.text: Finally $(x,y)B=(zt,t)B=tB$: both generators lie in $tB$, and the second generates $tB$. Since $j(y)=t$ and multiplication by $t$ is injective on $B$, injectivity of $j$ implies that multiplication by $y$ is injective on $R$. Thus the ideal extension and non-zero-divisor assertion use this same substitution, completing every clause.

lean.statement:
theorem integral_closure (F : Type u) [Field F] (a b c : F)
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hdisc : b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0) :
    ∃ j : CurveRing a b c →ₐ[F] PowerSeries (CoefficientAlgebra a b c),
      (∀ (H : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F) (n : ℕ),
        PowerSeries.coeff n (j (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {equation a b c}) H)) =
          ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
            algebraMap F (CoefficientAlgebra a b c)
              (MvPowerSeries.coeff (Finsupp.single 0 i + Finsupp.single 1 (n - i)) H) *
                AdjoinRoot.root (polynomial a b c) ^ i) ∧
      j (x a b c) = PowerSeries.C (AdjoinRoot.root (polynomial a b c)) * PowerSeries.X ∧
      j (y a b c) = PowerSeries.X ∧
      Function.Injective j ∧
      (∀ h : PowerSeries (CoefficientAlgebra a b c),
        (∃ r, j r = h) ↔
          ∃ d : F, ∃ g : PowerSeries (CoefficientAlgebra a b c),
            h = PowerSeries.C (algebraMap F (CoefficientAlgebra a b c) d) +
              PowerSeries.X * g) ∧
      IsReduced (CurveRing a b c) ∧
      @Module.Finite (CurveRing a b c) (PowerSeries (CoefficientAlgebra a b c)) _ _
        (@Algebra.toModule _ _ _ _ j.toRingHom.toAlgebra) ∧
      Ideal.map j.toRingHom (Ideal.span {x a b c, y a b c}) =
        Ideal.span {PowerSeries.X} ∧
      y a b c ∈ nonZeroDivisors (CurveRing a b c) ∧
      PowerSeries.X ∈ nonZeroDivisors (PowerSeries (CoefficientAlgebra a b c)) ∧
      ∃ k : PowerSeries (CoefficientAlgebra a b c) →+* FractionRing (CurveRing a b c),
        Function.Injective k ∧
        k.comp j.toRingHom = algebraMap (CurveRing a b c) (FractionRing (CurveRing a b c)) ∧
        (∀ w : FractionRing (CurveRing a b c),
          w ∈ integralClosure (CurveRing a b c) (FractionRing (CurveRing a b c)) ↔
            ∃ h : PowerSeries (CoefficientAlgebra a b c), k h = w)
